reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes a 2D HEA solid lubricant coating (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2, not an in situ phase formed from a precursor within a CoCrFeNi matrix. It does not address precursor incorporation, in situ transformation, or tribological performance of a CoCrFeNi-based alloy across the 25–800 °C range. Therefore, none of the key premises are supported by the cited passage.
premises: A precursor can be incorporated into CoCrFeNi to form a lubricious phase in situ during sliding.
The in situ phase will form a stable, low-shear tribofilm across room temperature to 800 °C.
This tribofilm will significantly reduce friction and wear compared to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The effect persists under moderate to high contact pressures and oxidizing environments.
